checkpoints.cue: A potato cube yields to a knife before the eggs are added.
checkpoints.why: The eggs can set before undercooked potatoes soften.

checkpoints.cue: Ground pork reaches 160°F, or ground poultry 165°F.
checkpoints.why: Browning alone does not establish the actual meat endpoint.

checkpoints.cue: The center in every casserole dish is set and reaches 165°F.
checkpoints.why: A golden edge can precede the center, especially with deep filling.

troubleshooting.problem: The eggs are set but the potatoes are hard
troubleshooting.cause: The potato cubes were large or insufficiently roasted before assembly.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep checking the casserole center and cover if the top darkens; next time test a potato cube before adding the eggs, rather than shortening the roast by its clock alone.

after.timing: The current original-batch plan is about 20 minutes preparation, 15–20 minutes potato roasting and 35–40 minutes egg baking, with skillet work overlapping the roast and a standing interval before slicing: about 1½ hours. Extra loads add elapsed time; no fixed rest or universal bake time is tested.

substitutions.alternative: Use the same listed meat amount as raw ground pork or raw poultry breakfast sausage. Read actual product instructions; check pork at 160°F or poultry at 165°F before assembly, and keep the casserole center check at 165°F.
substitutions.effect: Preserves the source-specific meat alternatives without equating cured or precooked sausage with raw ground meat.

substitutions.alternative: The current publisher also offers the same listed milk volume as whole milk, half-and-half or full-fat coconut milk instead of almond milk; choose one milk route and keep the rest of the complete formula.
substitutions.effect: These modern publisher alternatives change richness and flavor; the saved almond-milk main remains.

after.storage: Refrigerate cooked portions promptly in shallow containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F /32°C, at 40°F /4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days. Reheat portions to 165°F /74°C throughout, checking the center; cover if needed to keep the topping from over-browning.

exactBodyChange.before:
## Chef's Note

Small sweet-potato cubes roast before the egg mixture goes into the dish. That gives them time to soften without overbaking the eggs. Cook the sausage and wilt the spinach before assembling.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat oven to 400 degrees.

2. **Continue:** Place the sweet potatoes in a 9×13 inch casserole dish and then drizzle with avocado oil. Toss until well coated. Bake the sweet potatoes for 15-20 minutes until tender and then remove from the oven.

3. **Continue:** While the sweet potatoes are baking add the eggs, almond milk, green onion, hot sauce, salt, and pepper to a large mixing bowl. Whisk together until well combined and then fold in shredded cheese.

4. **Continue:** Next, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the sausage and brown, breaking it up as it cooks.

5. **Continue:** Once the sausage is brown add the onion, bell peppers, and garlic. Sauté for another 3-5 minutes or until onion and bell pepper start to become tender.

6. **Continue:** Add the baby spinach to the skillet, sauté for 30 seconds to 1 minute until the spinach is wilted, and then remove from the heat.

7. **Continue:** Give your casserole dish a light spray of olive or avocado oil to prevent sticking and then add the sausage mixture. Toss with the sweet potatoes until well combined.

8. **Continue:** Pour the egg mixture evenly over the sausage and veggies. Bake the casserole at 400 degrees for 35-40 (check after 30 minutes) until the egg is completely set. Let cool and then slice into 12 pieces. Use the listed avocado oil for the potatoes. Cook ground pork sausage to 160°F / 71°C, or poultry sausage to 165°F / 74°C. Bake the assembled casserole until its center reaches 165°F / 74°C.
exactBodyChange.after:
## Chef's Note

Roast the small sweet-potato cubes until tender before the eggs go in. Cook the sausage and wilt the spinach first, retaining their full mixture for the casserole. Spread the filling evenly, then bake until the center is set and reaches 165°F; a browned edge does not measure the middle.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Preheat the oven to 400°F. Wash the fresh vegetables before preparing them. Lightly grease an oven-safe 9×13-inch casserole dish for the original batch with the separate oil spray. Check its actual depth: when the full filling will not leave headroom, divide every ingredient among additional dishes before roasting or assembling, keeping similar depth.
2. **Roast potatoes:** Toss all the peeled 1/4-inch sweet-potato cubes with the full listed avocado oil in the prepared dish or dishes. Bake for about 15–20 minutes, until a cube in the center is tender when pierced; remove from the oven.
3. **Mix eggs:** While the potatoes roast, whisk all the eggs, almond milk, measured green onion, hot sauce, salt and pepper together. Fold in all the cheddar.
4. **Cook sausage:** Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add all the raw ground breakfast sausage or ground pork, breaking it up as it cooks. Cook ground pork to 160°F /71°C, or poultry sausage to 165°F /74°C; use raw ground sausage and follow its package instructions. Use additional skillet rounds if necessary rather than crowding it.
5. **Cook vegetables:** Add all the yellow onion, red and green bell peppers and garlic to the cooked sausage. Sauté for about 3–5 minutes, until the vegetables begin to soften. Reduce the heat if the garlic darkens before the vegetables soften.
6. **Wilt spinach:** Add all the spinach and stir for about 30 seconds to 1 minute, until wilted. Remove the skillet from the heat. Retain the full cooked sausage, vegetables and pan juices for assembly.
7. **Assemble:** Divide the full cooked skillet mixture among the roasted-potato dishes and toss together. Pour the egg mixture evenly over them, dividing all the eggs and filling among the dishes in the same proportions.
8. **Bake and serve:** Bake at 400°F for about 35–40 minutes, beginning checks at 30 minutes, until the egg center is set and reaches 165°F /74°C in each dish. A deeper load can take longer. Let stand until safe to handle and firm enough to slice, then cut into the listed planning count of slices. Add the separate optional extra green onion if desired.
